33

42	## Procedure

44	### 1. Resolve the ready set (the gate)
45	
46	Parse the selector from `$ARGUMENTS` (default `--status approved`):
47	
48	```
49	aida burndown plan --status approved --json     # or --tag <T> / --batch <B>
50	```
51	
52	This returns `{ ready: [...], awaiting_signoff: [...], parked: [{spec, reason}] }`.
53	**Only `ready` is fan-out-able.** `ready` is the advisor-blessed drain set:
54	queued + bounded + unblocked + decision-free — queue membership IS the advisor
55	sign-off (STORY-546), so the runner can never drain a spec the advisor didn't
56	deliberately queue. `awaiting_signoff` is pickable-but-unqueued (the advisor
57	hasn't blessed it yet) — report it but never act on it. Report the parked count
58	+ reasons once (so the operator sees what's held + why) but never act on parked

61	### 2. Fan out a wave (the engine)
62	
63	**First, drop any ready spec that's already in flight.** The gate is
64	pure/store-only — it can't see transient forge or session state, so a spec
65	mid-merge (open PR) or actively being worked (live session lease) can still come
66	back `ready`. Spawning a second implementer for it duplicates effort and races.
67	Before fanning out, filter the ready set against both:
68	
69	```
70	gh pr list --state open --json headRefName,title    # specs with an open PR
71	aida session leases                                  # specs with an active lease
72	```
73	
74	Skip any ready spec whose SPEC-ID matches an open PR branch/title or an active
75	lease scope; carry only the genuinely-idle remainder into the wave below.
76	
77	> **Do NOT invent a "competing drain" check beyond the two filters above.**
78	> When `AIDA_BURNDOWN_LOCK_HELD` is set in your environment, the launcher
79	> (`aida burndown run`) is already holding the **exclusive** drain lock — so by
80	> construction there is **no** other live drain or orchestrator racing this set.
81	> A `drain-state.json` you may see is either yours or a stale tombstone; do not
82	> read it and do not "hold to avoid double-driving." If a spec passes the
83	> open-PR + active-lease filters, **fan it out.** Treating the launcher's own
84	> lock/state as a competitor is the BUG-607 self-deadlock (the drain reports a
85	> live `pid …` that is actually its own parent and then refuses to do anything).

88	**worktree-isolated implementer subagent per spec**. **N = the `--concurrency`
89	value from `$ARGUMENTS` if provided** (so `aida burndown run --concurrency 6`
90	flows through), else `N ≈ 4` — or scale to budget:
91	
92	> `Agent(subagent_type: "general-purpose", isolation: "worktree")` — each gets
93	> ONE ready spec and a self-contained prompt: read it (`aida show <SPEC> -c`),
94	> **flip it in flight at pickup** (`aida edit <SPEC> --status in-progress`) so
95	> queue/status views agree the spec is being worked — the fanout lease alone
96	> doesn't flip it (BUG-754: `queue list` showed the same spec as both a
97	> pickable Approved row and in-flight/leased) — then
98	> implement to acceptance, add `// trace:<SPEC>` (plain `//`, never `///`),
99	> `cargo build` + `cargo test` + `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (check the exit
100	> code), commit `[AI:claude] type(scope): … (<SPEC>)` + the co-author trailer,
101	> push, open a PR, then mark the spec done (`aida queue done <SPEC>`) so it
102	> reaches **Done** and the normal merge-driven Done→Completed auto-bump fires on
103	> integration, and reply ONLY the PR URL or `BLOCKED: <reason>`.
104	
105	Worktree isolation means parallel agents never collide on files *mid-flight* —
106	but two specs that touch the SAME files still **conflict at MERGE time** (the
107	stacked / duplicate-edit hazard).
108	
109	**Sequential work in one worktree stacks branches (BUG-554).** The fan-out above
110	is safe because each subagent gets a FRESH worktree off `origin/main`. The hazard
111	is *reuse*: if a single agent (or you) works MORE THAN ONE spec in the SAME
112	worktree, branch each spec off `origin/main`, **never** off the current HEAD —
113	otherwise spec B's branch stacks on spec A's unmerged commit, which (1) pollutes
114	B's PR with A's commit and (2) makes A's commit reachable from two branches, so
115	`aida human` / `aida queue list` mis-attribute A to B's branch. Before each next
116	spec in a reused worktree: `git reset --hard origin/main` (or a fresh `git
117	worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/main`). `aida session start` already bases
118	on `origin/main` and warns when cwd is on a feature branch (BUG-76); raw `git`
119	does not — so this rule is on you when you drive `git` directly.
120	
121	**Route coupled file-sharing sets to a drain mode — do NOT fan them out in
122	parallel and do NOT hand-drive the reset.** The parallel fan-out (one worktree
123	per spec) is for INDEPENDENT specs. For a set that shares files / must land in
124	order, tag the members `batch:NAME` and drain the batch instead of fanning out:
125	
126	- **`aida queue work --batch NAME --auto-complete --sequential`** — ordered,
127	  each member is its OWN PR off freshly-pulled main, one member at a time
128	  (concurrency 1). A member failure **shelves** that member and the drain
129	  **continues** with the rest. Use when the members are coupled but each
130	  increment is independently shippable + reviewable.
131	- **`aida queue work --batch NAME --auto-complete --single-branch`** — all
132	  members accumulate on ONE shared branch in one worktree, no per-member
133	  merge-to-main, ONE cluster PR at the end. A member failure **halts** the drain
134	  (later increments build on earlier commits, so it stops rather than build on
135	  broken code). Use when the members must ship together.
136	
137	The one-line rule of thumb: **`--sequential` shelves-and-continues (independent
138	PRs); `--single-branch` halts (one accumulating branch).** Both replace the old
139	manual `git reset --hard origin/main` between members — let the mode base each
140	member correctly instead of driving `git` by hand. trace:BUG-554 trace:TASK-1005 | ai:claude
141	
142	**Never co-fan a serialize-group (STORY-614).** Specs that must not run
143	concurrently carry a shared `serialize:<group>` tag (e.g. `serialize:docs`,
144	`serialize:burndown-display`). When selecting the N specs for a wave, check each
145	ready spec's tags and include **AT MOST ONE** spec per `serialize:<group>` value;
146	the rest of that group drain in **successive** waves, after the first one lands
147	and merges. Independent specs still fan out in parallel — only the tagged
148	collision-set is serialized. This is the operator marking known file-overlap
149	("these touch the same code") so the drain enforces the ordering instead of
150	relying on someone remembering `--concurrency 1`. (A typed `ConflictsWith` edge
151	enforced in `resolve_burndown_sets` is the substrate-v2 follow-up — STORY-614;
152	the tag is the working slice.)
153	
154	### 3. Integrate (you are the integrator — do NOT implement)
155	
156	**Wait for each fanned-out PR's CI to reach a TERMINAL state before deciding its
157	fate — and never exit the drain while any PR is still pending (BUG-541).**
158	**Background watches do not exist in a headless session (BUG-755): the session
159	terminates when your turn ends, so a promised "background watch" dies with it
160	and the PR is silently orphaned. Never promise one — poll in the FOREGROUND
161	(`gh pr checks <n>`) and never end your turn while a wave PR is non-terminal or
162	blessed specs remain unstarted.** (The `aida burndown run` launcher relaunches a
163	continuation turn if a session exits with residual work — but that safety net is
164	recovery, not license to end the turn early.) A
165	PR's CI lags the implementer's push by minutes, so the LAST wave's PRs are
166	routinely still running when their implementer returns; treating "checks
167	pending" as "skip it" silently orphans the final PR (observed 2×: #852, #864
168	were stranded open+unmerged for the advisor to back-merge). For each returned
169	PR, poll `gh pr checks <n>` (or `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup`) until
170	it is **conclusive** — every required check SUCCESS or any FAILURE, not PENDING
171	— *before* merging or holding it. Do **not** declare the drain complete until
172	every PR it opened has reached a terminal state and been merged, held, or
173	explicitly listed as a straggler (step 6). The last PR is the one this bug
174	strands — give it the same wait every other PR got.
175	
176	For each returned PR: if all checks pass and it's mergeable + clean, merge it
177	(`--squash` only — NO `--delete-branch`: the implementer's worktree still holds
178	the branch, so the local delete is refused, and in an `&&` chain that silently
179	drops the pull leg) and then run `aida pull` as its own step — the spec was
180	marked **Done** by its implementer (step 2), so the merge-driven auto-bump
181	promotes it to **Completed** on pull. Branch deletion happens in the prune step
182	below, after the worktree is removed. As a fallback (e.g. the implementer skipped `queue done`, or the
183	auto-bump missed), run `aida db reconcile-status --spec <SPEC>` to force the
184	Completed bump. **Hold (do not merge) any PR whose spec is
185	`review:draft-only`** — leave it a draft for the operator. On a merge conflict,
186	have the agent rebase (`git merge origin/main`, resolve, push).
187	
188	**Prune the merged implementer worktree + branch (per merged spec).** After a
189	PR's merge succeeds **and** its spec auto-bumped to **Completed** (confirm with
190	`aida show <SPEC>` — status `Completed`), reclaim that implementer's
191	worktree-isolated branch and worktree. They are NOT cleaned up automatically:
192	`Agent(isolation: "worktree")` auto-cleans only **unchanged** worktrees, and a
193	committed + merged implementer worktree HAS changes, so it persists by design —
194	the integrator must prune it explicitly, or a long unattended drain accumulates
195	stale `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` worktrees that also block `git branch -d`.
196	
197	For each just-merged Completed spec:
198	
199	1. Identify the implementer's branch (the spec's own branch, e.g.
200	   `task-NNN-…` — the `headRefName` from the `gh pr list` entry) and its
201	   worktree path (the `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` or `~/ai/aida-<spec>` dir).
202	   `git worktree list --porcelain` maps branches → worktree paths.
203	2. Remove the worktree, then delete the local branch:
204	
205	   ```
206	   git worktree remove --force <that worktree path>
207	   git branch -d <that branch>            # -d = safe: refuses if not merged
208	   git push origin --delete <that branch> # remote cleanup (the merge deliberately skipped branch deletion)
209	   ```
210	
211	**Prune guards (follow these exactly — they bound the blast radius):**
212	
213	- **Completed-only.** ONLY prune a worktree whose spec reached **Completed**
214	  (i.e. its PR merged and the auto-bump landed). NEVER prune a worktree for a
215	  spec that is still held / `review:draft-only` / in-flight / `NeedsAttention` —
216	  that work is unmerged and the worktree is live.
217	- **Never the integrator's own tree.** NEVER `git worktree remove` the
218	  integrator's main worktree or the repo root — prune ONLY the implementer
219	  worktree that produced the just-merged PR.
220	- **Best-effort + non-fatal.** A worktree that won't remove (e.g. uncommitted
221	  unrelated changes from another agent) is **flagged and SKIPPED** — note it for
222	  the operator and continue. A prune failure must NEVER abort the wave or the
223	  loop; pruning is reclamation, not an integrity gate.
224	
225	**Verify the integrated `main` before looping (BUG-496).** After a wave's PRs
226	are merged, the merges are *integrated but un-tested together* — each PR's CI ran
227	against the **old** base, not the post-merge result, so two PRs that were green
228	alone can break `main` **together** (the squash-merge parallel-integration
229	hazard). So once a wave's PRs are merged: `git checkout main && git pull
230	--ff-only && cargo build -p aida-cli` (a quick compile is enough to catch the
231	usual integration breaks — a signature/import/type mismatch). **If it fails,
232	HALT the drain** — do **not** launch the next wave, and do **not** report
233	success. Fix-forward the break if it's mechanical, else park it and alert the
234	operator with the build error. **Never loop, and never declare "complete," over
235	a red `main`** — "every PR was green" is not "main is green" for a parallel wave.
236	
237	### 4. Punt-and-continue (non-negotiable)
238	
239	A blocker parks **one** spec — tag it + leave a note — and the pipeline rolls
240	on. One spec's failure must **never** halt the wave or the loop. **Never stop to
241	ask; never down tools.** A fork → make the defensible call or park that one
242	spec, then move to the next.
243	
244	### 5. Loop until drained
245	
246	Re-run `aida burndown plan` (the ready set shrinks as specs land + may grow as
247	blockers clear), launch the next wave, and repeat until `ready` is empty.
248	**Looping is not optional (BUG-755): stopping after wave 1 with blessed specs
249	unstarted is an incomplete drain.** Only a shelve/cap stop (`--max` reached, or
250	a shelved failure you are exiting non-zero over) may end the run with blessed
251	specs remaining — and then the report (step 6) must name them explicitly.
252	
253	For an **unattended** drain, wait on the wave **event-driven**, not on a blind
254	timer. Launch the harness `Monitor` tool over the drain's wake feed:
255	
256	```
257	Monitor(command: "aida watch --emit-wakes", persistent: true)
258	```
259	
260	`aida watch` tails the drain's event stream and prints a line **only** on an
261	actionable verb — a PR shipped or merged, a CI verdict, a punt, a shelve, the
262	queue drained — staying silent through the benign phase churn. The session burns
263	**zero tokens while the wave runs** and wakes exactly when there is something to
264	integrate, so supervision cost drops from O(time-elapsed) to O(actionable
265	events). Keep a **long-interval** `ScheduleWakeup` (e.g. 30–60 min) as the
266	documented degenerate fallback: if no event stream is live, or the watcher
267	wedges, the timer still resurfaces the loop — correctness never depends on the
268	event path.
269	
270	### 6. Report
271	
272	When the ready set is empty (or `--max` reached), report the drain on **two
273	channels** — they reach different audiences and neither replaces the other:
274	
275	1. **`PushNotification`** — the ambient at-the-keyboard ping (specs completed,
276	   parked-with-reason, worktrees that couldn't be pruned, what's left).
277	
278	2. **Post the completion summary to the advisor mailbox** so the *narrative* —
279	   the caveats and reasoning a `PushNotification` can't carry — lands in the
280	   advisor session's unread notice / inbox **without the operator relaying it.**
281	   Outcomes already reach the advisor automatically (merged PRs via the monitor,
282	   completed specs via the cache); what *doesn't* is the
283	   reasoning/caveats/escalations, so the operator has been cut-n-pasting every
284	   drain report. This step closes that paste loop — the burn-down analog of
285	   STORY-569's `--zen` clean-finish → review brief; same substrate-handoff
286	   principle, applied to the drain's completion report:
287	
288	   ```
289	   aida mailbox send --to advisor --intent handoff "Burn-down complete (<selector>).
290	
291	   Completed: <SPEC + PR url per landed spec>
292	   Caveats / verifications worth noting: <e.g. 'TASK-X passed CI but the integrated-main build was only a compile check'>
293	   Held / awaiting sign-off: <review:draft-only PRs left for the operator>
294	   Left for manual merge: <un-merged PRs — CI not yet terminal at exit, or an unresolved conflict; 'none' if the step-3 wait drained them all (BUG-541)>
295	   Parked (with reason): <spec + why, from the gate's parked set + any punt-and-continue parks>
296	   Worktrees not pruned: <flagged + skipped paths from step 3, if any>"
297	   ```
298	
299	   **Any un-merged PR MUST appear on the `Left for manual merge` line in BOTH
300	   channels (BUG-541).** If step 3 waited correctly this is normally `none`; but
301	   if a PR's CI was still pending at `--max`, or a conflict blocked the merge,
302	   name it explicitly (`#N <url>`) — silence reads as "all merged" and the PR is
303	   silently orphaned.
304	
305	   - Use `--intent handoff` for a normal completion report. Use
306	     `--intent request` instead if the summary contains something that needs an
307	     advisor **decision** (e.g. a parked spec the advisor must triage). Add
308	     `--urgent` only if the drain hit a `main`-breaking HALT (step 3) the advisor
309	     must see out-of-band.
310	   - Keep the body to the lines above — specs+PRs, caveats, held,
311	     parked-with-reason, unpruned worktrees. Omit a heading that has nothing
312	     under it (don't post empty lines). One message per completed drain.
313	   - **Best-effort:** a failed mailbox send must **never** retroactively fail an
314	     otherwise-complete drain — note it and continue.
315	
316	## Guardrails
317	
318	- **The gate is law.** Never fan out a spec `aida burndown plan` put in `parked`
319	  — it's parked because it needs a human (epic to decompose, pending decision,
320	  unsatisfied blocker, or a parking tag).
321	- **CI gates each PR — the integrated-`main` verify gates the wave.** A bad
322	  change parks (CI red → no merge), so no *single* bad PR reaches `main`. But CI
323	  ran each PR against the *old* base, so a parallel wave can still break `main`
324	  *together* (BUG-496) — the per-wave `cargo build` on integrated `main` (step 3)
325	  is what catches that. Both gates together are what let the integrator merge
326	  greens without re-reviewing each.
327	- **Keep at the keyboard, not the drain:** releases/tags and changes to the
328	  autonomy machinery itself (the orchestrator, this runner) ship supervised — a
329	  fix riding through a broken drain gets caught in the breakage.
330	
331	## Relationship to the orchestrator drain
332	
333	This is the **recommended** hands-off backlog-drain path. It deliberately uses
334	the harness's native subagent fan-out rather than `aida queue work
335	--auto-complete` (the orchestrator-spawns-agent path), which is hardened in
336	parallel. They are **not** competitors: reach for `/aida-burndown` to drain a
337	*ready set*; reach for the orchestrator drain when its single-spec lifecycle is
338	what you want. Don't run both against the same set.
339

> `cargo build` + `cargo test` + `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (check the exit
> code), commit `[AI:claude] type(scope): … (<SPEC>)` + the co-author trailer,
> push, open a PR, then mark the spec done (`aida queue done <SPEC>`) so it
> reaches **Done** and the normal merge-driven Done→Completed auto-bump fires on
> integration, and reply ONLY the PR URL or `BLOCKED: <reason>`.

Worktree isolation means parallel agents never collide on files *mid-flight* —
but two specs that touch the SAME files still **conflict at MERGE time** (the
stacked / duplicate-edit hazard).

**Sequential work in one worktree stacks branches (BUG-554).** The fan-out above
is safe because each subagent gets a FRESH worktree off `origin/main`. The hazard
is *reuse*: if a single agent (or you) works MORE THAN ONE spec in the SAME
worktree, branch each spec off `origin/main`, **never** off the current HEAD —
otherwise spec B's branch stacks on spec A's unmerged commit, which (1) pollutes
B's PR with A's commit and (2) makes A's commit reachable from two branches, so
`aida human` / `aida queue list` mis-attribute A to B's branch. Before each next
spec in a reused worktree: `git reset --hard origin/main` (or a fresh `git
worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/main`). `aida session start` already bases
on `origin/main` and warns when cwd is on a feature branch (BUG-76); raw `git`
does not — so this rule is on you when you drive `git` directly.

**Route coupled file-sharing sets to a drain mode — do NOT fan them out in
parallel and do NOT hand-drive the reset.** The parallel fan-out (one worktree
per spec) is for INDEPENDENT specs. For a set that shares files / must land in
order, tag the members `batch:NAME` and drain the batch instead of fanning out:

- **`aida queue work --batch NAME --auto-complete --sequential`** — ordered,
  each member is its OWN PR off freshly-pulled main, one member at a time
  (concurrency 1). A member failure **shelves** that member and the drain
  **continues** with the rest. Use when the members are coupled but each
  increment is independently shippable + reviewable.
- **`aida queue work --batch NAME --auto-complete --single-branch`** — all
  members accumulate on ONE shared branch in one worktree, no per-member
  merge-to-main, ONE cluster PR at the end. A member failure **halts** the drain
  (later increments build on earlier commits, so it stops rather than build on
  broken code). Use when the members must ship together.

The one-line rule of thumb: **`--sequential` shelves-and-continues (independent
PRs); `--single-branch` halts (one accumulating branch).** Both replace the old
manual `git reset --hard origin/main` between members — let the mode base each
member correctly instead of driving `git` by hand. trace:BUG-554 trace:TASK-1005 | ai:claude

**Never co-fan a serialize-group (STORY-614).** Specs that must not run
concurrently carry a shared `serialize:<group>` tag (e.g. `serialize:docs`,
`serialize:burndown-display`). When selecting the N specs for a wave, check each
ready spec's tags and include **AT MOST ONE** spec per `serialize:<group>` value;
the rest of that group drain in **successive** waves, after the first one lands
and merges. Independent specs still fan out in parallel — only the tagged
collision-set is serialized. This is the operator marking known file-overlap
("these touch the same code") so the drain enforces the ordering instead of
relying on someone remembering `--concurrency 1`. (A typed `ConflictsWith` edge
enforced in `resolve_burndown_sets` is the substrate-v2 follow-up — STORY-614;
the tag is the working slice.)

### 3. Integrate (you are the integrator — do NOT implement)

**Wait for each fanned-out PR's CI to reach a TERMINAL state before deciding its
fate — and never exit the drain while any PR is still pending (BUG-541).**
**Background watches do not exist in a headless session (BUG-755): the session
terminates when your turn ends, so a promised "background watch" dies with it
and the PR is silently orphaned. Never promise one — poll in the FOREGROUND
(`gh pr checks <n>`) and never end your turn while a wave PR is non-terminal or
blessed specs remain unstarted.** (The `aida burndown run` launcher relaunches a
continuation turn if a session exits with residual work — but that safety net is
recovery, not license to end the turn early.) A
PR's CI lags the implementer's push by minutes, so the LAST wave's PRs are
routinely still running when their implementer returns; treating "checks
pending" as "skip it" silently orphans the final PR (observed 2×: #852, #864
were stranded open+unmerged for the advisor to back-merge). For each returned
PR, poll `gh pr checks <n>` (or `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup`) until
it is **conclusive** — every required check SUCCESS or any FAILURE, not PENDING
— *before* merging or holding it. Do **not** declare the drain complete until
every PR it opened has reached a terminal state and been merged, held, or
explicitly listed as a straggler (step 6). The last PR is the one this bug
strands — give it the same wait every other PR got.

For each returned PR: if all checks pass and it's mergeable + clean, merge it
(`--squash` only — NO `--delete-branch`: the implementer's worktree still holds
the branch, so the local delete is refused, and in an `&&` chain that silently
drops the pull leg) and then run `aida pull` as its own step — the spec was
marked **Done** by its implementer (step 2), so the merge-driven auto-bump
promotes it to **Completed** on pull. Branch deletion happens in the prune step
below, after the worktree is removed. As a fallback (e.g. the implementer skipped `queue done`, or the
auto-bump missed), run `aida db reconcile-status --spec <SPEC>` to force the
Completed bump. **Hold (do not merge) any PR whose spec is
`review:draft-only`** — leave it a draft for the operator. On a merge conflict,
have the agent rebase (`git merge origin/main`, resolve, push).

**Prune the merged implementer worktree + branch (per merged spec).** After a
PR's merge succeeds **and** its spec auto-bumped to **Completed** (confirm with
`aida show <SPEC>` — status `Completed`), reclaim that implementer's
worktree-isolated branch and worktree. They are NOT cleaned up automatically:
`Agent(isolation: "worktree")` auto-cleans only **unchanged** worktrees, and a
committed + merged implementer worktree HAS changes, so it persists by design —
the integrator must prune it explicitly, or a long unattended drain accumulates
stale `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` worktrees that also block `git branch -d`.

For each just-merged Completed spec:

1. Identify the implementer's branch (the spec's own branch, e.g.
   `task-NNN-…` — the `headRefName` from the `gh pr list` entry) and its
   worktree path (the `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` or `~/ai/aida-<spec>` dir).
   `git worktree list --porcelain` maps branches → worktree paths.
2. Remove the worktree, then delete the local branch:

   ```
   git worktree remove --force <that worktree path>
   git branch -d <that branch>            # -d = safe: refuses if not merged
   git push origin --delete <that branch> # remote cleanup (the merge deliberately skipped branch deletion)
   ```

**Prune guards (follow these exactly — they bound the blast radius):**

- **Completed-only.** ONLY prune a worktree whose spec reached **Completed**
  (i.e. its PR merged and the auto-bump landed). NEVER prune a worktree for a
  spec that is still held / `review:draft-only` / in-flight / `NeedsAttention` —
  that work is unmerged and the worktree is live.
- **Never the integrator's own tree.** NEVER `git worktree remove` the
  integrator's main worktree or the repo root — prune ONLY the implementer
  worktree that produced the just-merged PR.
- **Best-effort + non-fatal.** A worktree that won't remove (e.g. uncommitted
  unrelated changes from another agent) is **flagged and SKIPPED** — note it for
  the operator and continue. A prune failure must NEVER abort the wave or the
  loop; pruning is reclamation, not an integrity gate.

**Verify the integrated `main` before looping (BUG-496).** After a wave's PRs
are merged, the merges are *integrated but un-tested together* — each PR's CI ran
against the **old** base, not the post-merge result, so two PRs that were green
alone can break `main` **together** (the squash-merge parallel-integration
hazard). So once a wave's PRs are merged: `git checkout main && git pull
--ff-only && cargo build -p aida-cli` (a quick compile is enough to catch the
usual integration breaks — a signature/import/type mismatch). **If it fails,
HALT the drain** — do **not** launch the next wave, and do **not** report
success. Fix-forward the break if it's mechanical, else park it and alert the
operator with the build error. **Never loop, and never declare "complete," over
a red `main`** — "every PR was green" is not "main is green" for a parallel wave.

### 4. Punt-and-continue (non-negotiable)

A blocker parks **one** spec — tag it + leave a note — and the pipeline rolls
on. One spec's failure must **never** halt the wave or the loop. **Never stop to
ask; never down tools.** A fork → make the defensible call or park that one
spec, then move to the next.

### 5. Loop until drained

Re-run `aida burndown plan` (the ready set shrinks as specs land + may grow as
blockers clear), launch the next wave, and repeat until `ready` is empty.
**Looping is not optional (BUG-755): stopping after wave 1 with blessed specs
unstarted is an incomplete drain.** Only a shelve/cap stop (`--max` reached, or
a shelved failure you are exiting non-zero over) may end the run with blessed
specs remaining — and then the report (step 6) must name them explicitly.

For an **unattended** drain, wait on the wave **event-driven**, not on a blind
timer. Launch the harness `Monitor` tool over the drain's wake feed:

```
Monitor(command: "aida watch --emit-wakes", persistent: true)
```

`aida watch` tails the drain's event stream and prints a line **only** on an
actionable verb — a PR shipped or merged, a CI verdict, a punt, a shelve, the
queue drained — staying silent through the benign phase churn. The session burns
**zero tokens while the wave runs** and wakes exactly when there is something to
integrate, so supervision cost drops from O(time-elapsed) to O(actionable
events). Keep a **long-interval** `ScheduleWakeup` (e.g. 30–60 min) as the
documented degenerate fallback: if no event stream is live, or the watcher
wedges, the timer still resurfaces the loop — correctness never depends on the
event path.

### 6. Report

When the ready set is empty (or `--max` reached), report the drain on **two
channels** — they reach different audiences and neither replaces the other:

1. **`PushNotification`** — the ambient at-the-keyboard ping (specs completed,
   parked-with-reason, worktrees that couldn't be pruned, what's left).

2. **Post the completion summary to the advisor mailbox** so the *narrative* —
   the caveats and reasoning a `PushNotification` can't carry — lands in the
   advisor session's unread notice / inbox **without the operator relaying it.**
   Outcomes already reach the advisor automatically (merged PRs via the monitor,
   completed specs via the cache); what *doesn't* is the
   reasoning/caveats/escalations, so the operator has been cut-n-pasting every
   drain report. This step closes that paste loop — the burn-down analog of
   STORY-569's `--zen` clean-finish → review brief; same substrate-handoff
   principle, applied to the drain's completion report:

   ```
   aida mailbox send --to advisor --intent handoff "Burn-down complete (<selector>).

   Completed: <SPEC + PR url per landed spec>
   Caveats / verifications worth noting: <e.g. 'TASK-X passed CI but the integrated-main build was only a compile check'>
   Held / awaiting sign-off: <review:draft-only PRs left for the operator>
   Left for manual merge: <un-merged PRs — CI not yet terminal at exit, or an unresolved conflict; 'none' if the step-3 wait drained them all (BUG-541)>
   Parked (with reason): <spec + why, from the gate's parked set + any punt-and-continue parks>
   Worktrees not pruned: <flagged + skipped paths from step 3, if any>"
   ```

   **Any un-merged PR MUST appear on the `Left for manual merge` line in BOTH
   channels (BUG-541).** If step 3 waited correctly this is normally `none`; but
   if a PR's CI was still pending at `--max`, or a conflict blocked the merge,
   name it explicitly (`#N <url>`) — silence reads as "all merged" and the PR is
   silently orphaned.

   - Use `--intent handoff` for a normal completion report. Use
     `--intent request` instead if the summary contains something that needs an
     advisor **decision** (e.g. a parked spec the advisor must triage). Add
     `--urgent` only if the drain hit a `main`-breaking HALT (step 3) the advisor
     must see out-of-band.
   - Keep the body to the lines above — specs+PRs, caveats, held,
     parked-with-reason, unpruned worktrees. Omit a heading that has nothing
     under it (don't post empty lines). One message per completed drain.
   - **Best-effort:** a failed mailbox send must **never** retroactively fail an
     otherwise-complete drain — note it and continue.

## Guardrails

- **The gate is law.** Never fan out a spec `aida burndown plan` put in `parked`
  — it's parked because it needs a human (epic to decompose, pending decision,
  unsatisfied blocker, or a parking tag).
- **CI gates each PR — the integrated-`main` verify gates the wave.** A bad
  change parks (CI red → no merge), so no *single* bad PR reaches `main`. But CI
  ran each PR against the *old* base, so a parallel wave can still break `main`
  *together* (BUG-496) — the per-wave `cargo build` on integrated `main` (step 3)
  is what catches that. Both gates together are what let the integrator merge
  greens without re-reviewing each.
- **Keep at the keyboard, not the drain:** releases/tags and changes to the
  autonomy machinery itself (the orchestrator, this runner) ship supervised — a
  fix riding through a broken drain gets caught in the breakage.

## Relationship to the orchestrator drain

This is the **recommended** hands-off backlog-drain path. It deliberately uses
the harness's native subagent fan-out rather than `aida queue work
--auto-complete` (the orchestrator-spawns-agent path), which is hardened in
parallel. They are **not** competitors: reach for `/aida-burndown` to drain a
*ready set*; reach for the orchestrator drain when its single-spec lifecycle is
what you want. Don't run both against the same set.

200	# provenance on one leaks the developer breadcrumb into user-facing output
201	# (BUG-227 / TASK-268's "both-at-once trap"). The CI test
202	# source_doc_comments_carry_no_spec_id_provenance catches it minutes later; this
203	# gate catches it at the moment of writing.

205	# A line is *provenance* — and rejected — when it carries a `trace:` marker, OR
206	# is a *bare* SPEC-ID (essentially nothing but SPEC-ID token(s) + punctuation,
207	# no descriptive prose words). A *descriptive* mention of a SPEC-ID inside prose
208	# (e.g. `/// reuses the STORY-122 usage log`) is legitimate help text, NOT a
209	# leak, and is allowed (BUG-629 tightened this from the old over-broad "any

212	# helper — keep the two in lockstep (TASK-903).

219	# --no-verify, which ALSO skips the advisor-code-gate above, defeating both

221	# content lines (excluding the `+++ b/file` header), so only NEWLY-added `///`

223	# diff-filtered out.

229	# returns 1 (allow) for a descriptive prose mention or no SPEC-ID at all.

232	    # No SPEC-ID at all → nothing to leak.

234	    # A `trace:` marker on a `///` line is always provenance.
235	    case "$docline" in *trace:*) return 0 ;; esac
236	    # Strip the leading `///`, then delete every SPEC-ID token. If an alphabetic

238	    # Otherwise only punctuation/digits remain → bare SPEC-ID → reject.

#!/bin/bash
# TASK-144: the pre-commit `///`-provenance gate must not false-positive on
# PURE MOVES. The gate (TASK-135/BUG-624/BUG-629/TASK-903) scans added diff
# lines only, so a mechanical file-split used to re-add pre-existing
# `/// trace:` debt and refuse the commit (~85 false-flagged lines during the
# STORY-771 extraction) even though BUG-624's design note says debt a commit
# did not introduce must not block it. The fix credits `-`-removed provenance
# lines in the SAME staged diff against added candidates (trim-insensitive,
# counted), so a move is excused while genuinely NEW debt is still refused.
#
# Drives the REAL template (aida-core/templates/hooks/aida-pre-commit.sh)
# installed as .git/hooks/pre-commit in a throwaway repo, via real `git commit`.
#
# trace:TASK-144 | ai:claude
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
HOOK_TEMPLATE="$PROJECT_ROOT/aida-core/templates/hooks/aida-pre-commit.sh"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
FAKEHOME=$(mktemp -d)
STDERR_LOG="$FAKEHOME/stderr.txt"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP" "$FAKEHOME"' EXIT
fail=0

cd "$TMP"
git init -q -b main
git config user.email t@t.t
git config user.name t
mkdir -p .git/hooks src
cp "$HOOK_TEMPLATE" .git/hooks/pre-commit
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

# commit <msg> — run a real hermetic `git commit` (FAKEHOME so no user config /
# aida state leaks in; no AIDA_SESSION_ROLE so the advisor-code-gate, if an
# aida binary is even resolvable, allows). Echoes the exit code; stderr is
# captured OUTSIDE the repo so `git add -A` never stages it.
commit() {
    set +e
    env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$FAKEHOME" \
        git -c user.email=t@t.t -c user.name=t commit -qm "$1" \
        >/dev/null 2>"$STDERR_LOG"
    local rc=$?
    set -e
    echo "$rc"
}

assert_exit() {
    local desc="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
    if [ "$actual" -eq "$expected" ]; then
        echo "ok   - $desc (exit $actual)"
    else
        echo "FAIL - $desc (expected $expected, got $actual)"
        [ -s "$STDERR_LOG" ] && sed 's/^/       | /' "$STDERR_LOG"
        fail=1
    fi
}

assert_stderr_contains() {
    local desc="$1" needle="$2"
    if grep -q "$needle" "$STDERR_LOG"; then
        echo "ok   - $desc"
    else
        echo "FAIL - $desc (stderr lacks '$needle')"
        fail=1
    fi
}

assert_stderr_lacks() {
    local desc="$1" needle="$2"
    if grep -q "$needle" "$STDERR_LOG"; then
        echo "FAIL - $desc (stderr unexpectedly contains '$needle')"
        fail=1
    else
        echo "ok   - $desc"
    fi
}

# --no-verify, exactly how such debt predates the gate).
cat >src/lib.rs <<'EOF'
/// trace:TASK-101 | ai:claude
pub fn alpha() {}
/// trace:TASK-102 | ai:claude
pub fn beta() {}
pub fn gamma() {}
EOF

cat >src/lib.rs <<'EOF'
pub fn gamma() {}
EOF
cat >src/split.rs <<'EOF'
/// trace:TASK-101 | ai:claude
pub fn alpha() {}
/// trace:TASK-102 | ai:claude
pub fn beta() {}
EOF
git add -A
assert_exit "pure file-split move of /// trace debt is allowed" 0 "$(commit "refactor: split")"

# 2. GENUINELY NEW debt (no matching staged removal) → still REFUSED.
cat >>src/split.rs <<'EOF'
/// trace:BUG-999 | ai:claude
pub fn delta() {}
EOF
git add -A
assert_exit "genuinely new /// trace debt is refused" 1 "$(commit "feat: new debt")"
assert_stderr_contains "refusal names the new debt line" "BUG-999"
git reset -q --hard

# 3. MOVE + NEW debt in one commit → REFUSED, but ONLY the new line is flagged;
#    the moved line is excused.
cat >src/lib.rs <<'EOF'

pub fn gamma() {}
EOF
cat >src/split.rs <<'EOF'

EOF
git add -A
assert_exit "move mixed with new debt is refused" 1 "$(commit "feat: mixed")"
assert_stderr_contains "refusal flags the new line" "BUG-777"
assert_stderr_lacks "refusal does NOT flag the moved line" "TASK-101"

pub mod inner {
    /// trace:TASK-102 | ai:claude

}
EOF
cat >src/split.rs <<'EOF'

#    the duplicate beyond the removal count is NEW debt → REFUSED.

pub mod inner {
    pub fn beta() {}
}
EOF

/// trace:TASK-102 | ai:claude

/// trace:TASK-102 | ai:claude
pub fn zeta() {}
EOF
git add -A
assert_exit "duplicating a moved line beyond its removal count is refused" 1 "$(commit "feat: dup")"
